changes: Issue 688 (R244): the two bow intakes are blind wells through the bow housing, with the kit's rolled lips, lip bolts, three inset rings and dark rear baffles exposed; the redundant smooth liners are removed and the bow loot locker sits behind the wells

Ryan, Nov 14: the front circles should be open holes with detail, never just circles. The solid bow block had capped both kit tubes immediately behind their lips. They remain fuel and dust intakes, not extra weapons (data.js c_hulk has only the two turrets)

Issue 688 (R244): the slab has 0.7 to 0.92 upper chamfers, lower chines, diagonal shoulders into a 0.3-per-side recessed waist, and four tapered starboard armour wedges with offset ledges; flank fittings and hard points follow the new skin

Ryan, Nov 14: the sides were flat walls, unlike the angular concept. The carrier keeps its broad deck, forward hangar mouths (R239), two raised turrets clear of sensors (R240), five stern engines and Carrier class length 16.5

Issue 668 (R239): both hangar mouths open forward in the bow face, one either side of the bow block beside the twin tubes (port 1.36 wide, starboard 1.32; 1.72 high; 3.0 deep to the back wall, 2.7 to the blast door), framed by a sill, a lintel and an outer cheek each; the port flank is closed plate now

Ryan, Nov 13 2026 (R239), on A20 painted and widened: "on the hullbreakers carrier, I was wrong. I prefer the concepts version of the bays facing forward now that I see it built." The beauty and the sheet's bow-on view draw the two mouths in the bow face beside the twin tubes with a craft visible inside; this replaces his Nov 12 port-flank ruling (issue 633). The layout is the closed PR 658's (commit 98e39958), on issue 651's 3.2 half-beam; data.js c_hulk (launch, hangar 2) is met either way

Each mouth is a real recess with a worn torn plate rim, dark launch rails on the floor, dark ceiling beams and frame ribs at uneven spacing, three small warm deck lights at uneven depths and an inner blast door on the back wall; no door leaves (issue 668, R240)

the Board's brief: they must read as launch bays with depth; in the bow face there is no face beside a mouth for designs.md's slid doors (the bow block stands there), so the kit part leaves them out (hangar_mouth doors=False). R240 (Ryan, Nov 13 2026: "some sort of weird paint pattern in the opening of the carrier"): the striped iron fit-out, the evenly spaced rail ties and the red lamps are gone; the fit-out is dark, only the rim carries worn iron edging (stack zone iron_edge), the deck lights are warm (glow zone lamp)
The mouths are lined dark (floor, ceiling, back wall and ends): only the worn rim, the few warm deck lights and the fighters catch the light

the Board on round 1 (Nov 13): the mouths must be big, deep, dark openings that show from the beauty camera with the fighter in them; round 1's were 1.37 high and lit grey inside, so they read as shallow grilles

The bow block is as tall as the slab and about half its beam (3.2 across, 1.9 tall, 2.7 long); its face carries two huge intake tubes side by side, each 1.1 across (three quarters of the face's height), reaching 2.3 back into the block

the Board on round 1 (Nov 13): the build had no twin tubes (two 0.8 tubes in a narrow block); the README's bow intakes and the beauty's two huge tubes. The concept sheet's plan draws the block about 0.4 of the beam; it is widened so the tubes fit side by side
Bow thrusters and the bow lamps on the bow block's flanks, the chin scoop under the web between the tubes
the wider block and its tubes fill the old places
The two shoulder dishes stand on the lintels over the mouths
designs.md puts the dishes on the shoulders; the mouths took the shoulders' faces (issue 668)
The slab is 6.4 wide over its hull (hull length to beam 2.58 on the top view) and 2.05 deep; issue 668 keeps issue 651's beam
the accepted beauty (v2s, "hull deepened") draws it about 2.4 long for its width, the sheet's top view 3.4; issue 651 broadened it toward the beauty's broad slab (R229: the whole concept; R233, R236)
Two dorsal turrets, one on the fore deck tier and one on the aft
data.js c_hulk: turret T twice (R221); designs.md's bow casemates, starboard flank guns and rocket rack have no slot, so they are not built

designs.md and the beauty (the fighter in the near mouth); the game's squadron length gives the scale
The spare engine bell lies across the deck in a cradle, cold
the picture's bell on the deck; designs.md: bolted down flat (field repairs)
The salvage deck is three low tiers of stacked plate with lockers bolted down, not loose junk
Ryan R185: nothing hangs off the ship; stacked and bolted scrap brick (R196, R197)
One pair of grabbers under the bow block and two heavy grapple arms folded flat under the stern quarters
designs.md (four bow arms become two, so the jaw is not A17's; the grapples drag prizes alongside)
Four attitude thrusters
a ship in space needs them to turn
The fore weld B-1 moved aft to x 2.3, behind the mouths' back wall (issue 668; was 4.75)

with the mouths in the bow face a weld at 4.75 would cut through both mouths and the port fighter; the bow, both mouths and their craft now tear away as one piece (designs.md: the bay side tears first)

Every face is plated in courses at the hull's plate size (0.4 to 0.9), each course jointed on its own (a brick bond), patches laid over joints and offset patches over plates; upward faces stepped in terraces of one to three plate thicknesses

the Board on round 1 (Nov 13): the faces read as big smooth grey planes with a few greebles; the concept is scrap brick, plates over plates on every face (R196, R197). Kit: the sheet kit's courses plating (kit.py, opt-in, issue 633)
Insides: two hangar deck levels behind each mouth, loot holds in the bow and in the core between the mouths, a kennel deck, the core between the hangar decks, machinery and the engine room aft
designs.md; R209, R215
